correctness.rationale: Every vertex has closed neighborhood size four, yielding the sharp lower bound. Explicit singleton words attain it. An incidence-excess argument excludes double columns for odd n, and perfect coverage excludes them for lengths divisible by four. Empty columns cannot be consecutive; counting gaps and forced opposite colors gives all optimal words. A complete case analysis of one-token differences gives exactly two jumps for odd n, with permutation (i,x)->(i-2,complement x), a single 2n-cycle. Row equality decides slides by n modulo four. n=3 and n divisible by four have separately proved graphs. Direct exhaustive bitmask and independent word-model checkers reproduce all claimed small instances.

value.rationale: This is a natural connectedness and motion-cost classification for optimal monitoring on a standard cubic Cartesian product. It separates 2n isolated slide configurations from a diameter-n jump cycle in one infinite residue class, and yields the same cycle under both moves in its neighboring odd class; lengths divisible by four give the zero-defect frozen comparison. Such exact motion constraints are not implied by counts of minimum sets and are useful for benchmarking domination reconfiguration.
